```{.r .cell-code}
#############################################
### clean and de-dup child dataframe
### this is our base demo file for the sample

child_clean <- child %>% 
  distinct(unique_id,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### no records dropped

  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  mutate(race_clean = case_when(
    race=="Asian or Pacific Islander" & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 1,
    race=="Black" & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 2,
    ethnicity=="Hispanic" ~ 3,
    race=="White" & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 4,
    race %in% c("Unknown","American Indian or Alaskan Native") & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_clean = factor(race_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5),
         labels = c("Asian", "Black", "Hispanic", "White", "Other"))) %>% 
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when(
    gender=="Female" ~ 1,
    gender=="Male" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("Female", "Male"))) %>% 
  ### clean dates
  mutate(birth_date = ymd(as_date(birth_date)))
```

```{.r .cell-code}
#############################################

supervision_clean <- supervision %>% 
  distinct(unique_id,
           referral_number,
           supervision_begin_date,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### 1 record dropped (note: 170 records have duplicated IDs but different begin dates)
  ### clean dates and create years for potential grouping in future trend analysis
  mutate(supervision_begin_date = ymd(as_date(supervision_begin_date)),
         supervision_end_date = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date)),
         supervision_begin_year = year(supervision_begin_date),
         supervision_end_year = year(supervision_end_date),
         overall_supervision_los_days = as.numeric(difftime(supervision_end_date,
                                                            supervision_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days"))) %>% 
    group_by(unique_id,
           referral_number) |> 
  mutate(overall_supervision_los_days_min_max = sum(overall_supervision_los_days)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  ### create unique referral ID possible filtering, joining, or counting
  mutate(unique_referral_id = paste0(unique_id,
                                     referral_number),
         unique_supervision_id = paste0(unique_id,
                                        referral_number,
                                        supervision_begin_date)) %>% 
  ### count number of supervision periods per referral 
  group_by(unique_referral_id) |> 
  mutate(supervision_periods_per_referral = n_distinct(unique_supervision_id,
                                          na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  ### and number of referrals per youth
  group_by(unique_id) |> 
  mutate(referrals_per_youth = n_distinct(unique_referral_id,
                                          na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  ### rename columns with duplicate names across files to indicate where data initially came from 
  dplyr::rename(supervision_disposition = disposition,
                supervision_outcome = outcome)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
#############################################
### clean and de-dup supervision_level dataframe
#############################################

### by unique_id, referral_number, phase_begin_date, phase_end_date
supervision_level_clean <- supervision_level %>% 
  distinct(unique_id,
           referral_number,
           phase,
           phase_begin_date,
           phase_end_date,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>%  ### 1 record dropped 
  ### clean dates and create years for potential grouping in future trend analysis
  mutate(phase_begin_date = ymd(as_date(phase_begin_date)),
         phase_end_date = ymd(as_date(phase_end_date)),
         unique_supervision_id = paste0(unique_id,
                                        referral_number,
                                        supervision_begin_date)) %>% 
  ### rename columns with duplicate names across files to indicate where data initially came from 
  dplyr::rename(supervision_level_phase = phase,
                supervision_level_supervision_type = supervision_type,
                supervision_level_phase_begin_date = phase_begin_date,
                supervision_level_phase_end_date = phase_end_date) %>% 
  ### create hierarchy of supervision levels
  ### when we measure changes/modifications to supervision levels,
  ### we are most interested in changes to more intensive levels of supervision 
  ### (as opposed to planned decreases in intensity over time)
    mutate(supervision_level_phase_severity = 
           case_when(
             supervision_level_phase=="PLACEMENT" ~ 1,
             supervision_level_phase=="DETENTION/SHELTER" ~ 2,
             supervision_level_phase=="ISP LEVEL 1" ~ 3,             
             supervision_level_phase=="ISP LEVEL 2" ~ 4,
             supervision_level_phase=="ISP LEVEL 3" ~ 5,
             supervision_level_phase=="PROB LEVEL R1" ~ 6,
             supervision_level_phase=="PROB LEVEL R2" ~ 7,             
             supervision_level_phase=="PROB LEVEL R3" ~ 8,
             supervision_level_phase=="PROB LEVEL R4" ~ 9,
             supervision_level_phase%in%c("None","WARRANT") ~ 11, 
             TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>% 
  ### now arrange and group by youth to take the next supervision level, if present
  ### using dplyr::lead to take the next supervision_level_phase_severity value
  ### using https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/lead-lag.html
  ### this will allow us to calculate the number of instances where youth 
  ### experienced an increase in supervision intensiveness 
  ### logic: using supervision_level_phase_severity, next value is less than current value
  ### indicates an increase in intensity of supervision
  arrange(unique_id,
          referral_number,
          supervision_level_phase_begin_date) %>%
  group_by(unique_id,
           referral_number) %>%
  mutate(next_supervision_level = dplyr::lead(supervision_level_phase_severity,
                                                   1,
                                                   default=NA)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(next_supervision_level_is_increase_flag = ifelse(supervision_level_phase_severity>next_supervision_level,
                                                          1,0)) %>% 
  ### calculate los by supervision level type (probation, detention, placement, none, and warrant)
  mutate(overall_supervision_los_days = as.numeric(difftime(supervision_end_date,
                                                            supervision_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days")),
         temp_supervision_level_los_days = as.numeric(difftime(supervision_level_phase_end_date,
                                                            supervision_level_phase_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days"))) %>% 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id) %>% 
  mutate(probation_supervision_los_days = sum(temp_supervision_level_los_days[supervision_level_phase%in%c("ISP LEVEL 1",
                                                                                                        "ISP LEVEL 2",
                                                                                                        "ISP LEVEL 3",
                                                                                                        "PROB LEVEL R1",
                                                                                                        "PROB LEVEL R2",
                                                                                                        "PROB LEVEL R3",
                                                                                                        "PROB LEVEL R4")],
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         detention_supervision_los_days = sum(temp_supervision_level_los_days[supervision_level_phase=="DETENTION/SHELTER"],
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         placement_supervision_los_days = sum(temp_supervision_level_los_days[supervision_level_phase=="PLACEMENT"],
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         none_supervision_los_days = sum(temp_supervision_level_los_days[supervision_level_phase=="NONE"],
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         warrant_supervision_los_days = sum(temp_supervision_level_los_days[supervision_level_phase=="WARRANT"],
                                              na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ### create a count variable in case it's handy for later analysis
  ### sum los by supervision phase/level type at supervision record-level 
  mutate(overall_unique_supervision_levels_per_supervision_episode_count = n_distinct(unique_id,
                                                           referral_number,
                                                           supervision_level_phase_begin_date,
                                                           supervision_level_phase_end_date),
         supervision_level_increases_per_supervision_episode_count = sum(next_supervision_level_is_increase_flag,
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         probation_supervision_los_days = sum(probation_supervision_los_days,
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         detention_supervision_los_days = sum(detention_supervision_los_days,
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         placement_supervision_los_days = sum(placement_supervision_los_days,
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         none_supervision_los_days = sum(none_supervision_los_days,
                                              na.rm = TRUE),
         warrant_supervision_los_days = sum(warrant_supervision_los_days,
                                              na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ### de-dup, keeping first record to preserve initial level for supervision period
  arrange(unique_supervision_id,
          supervision_level_phase_begin_date) %>% 
  distinct(unique_supervision_id,
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  ### only keeping variables created at supervision record-level
  dplyr::select(unique_supervision_id,
                initial_supervision_level = supervision_level_phase,
                overall_supervision_los_days,
                overall_unique_supervision_levels_per_supervision_episode_count,
                supervision_level_increases_per_supervision_episode_count,
                probation_supervision_los_days:warrant_supervision_los_days)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
#############################################
### clean and de-dup offenses dataframe

offenses_clean <- offenses %>% 
  distinct(unique_id,
           referral_number,
           offense_id,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### no records dropped
  ### clean dates and create years for potential grouping in future trend analysis
  mutate(offense_date = ymd(as_date(offense_date)),
         referral_date = ymd(as_date(referral_date)),
         disposition_date = ymd(as_date(disposition_date)),
         offense_year = year(offense_date),
         referral_year = year(referral_date),
         offense_disposition_year = year(disposition_date)) %>% 
  ### create unique referral ID and unique offense ID for possible filtering or counting
  mutate(unique_referral_id = paste0(unique_id,
                                     referral_number),
         unique_offense_id = paste0(unique_id,
                                    referral_number,
                                    offense_id)) %>% 
  ### calculate number of offenses per referral by grouping by unique_referral_id
  group_by(unique_referral_id) %>% 
  mutate(unique_offenses_per_referral_count = n_distinct(unique_offense_id,
                                                         na.rm = TRUE),
```

## Join 6. Join of `supervision_child_join_offenses_5` and `violations_clean_de_dup`


**Logic to double check:** only keeping violation records where the violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
### left join of violations_clean file to supervision_child_join_offenses_5 file 
supervision_child_join_offenses_violatons_6 <- 
  left_join(supervision_child_join_offenses_5,
            violations_clean_de_dup,
            by = c("unique_id")) %>% ### this is a many to many join so there are now lots of records (all violations joining to all supervisions/supervision extensions/supervision levels)
  ### now we need to filter on date -- only keeping violation records where the violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date
  ### first create fake end date for records where the end date is blank; since this indicates that supervision was ongoing at time of data pull, we still want to include violations that occurred so changing NA to '2030-01-01' in new variable for the following filter
  mutate(supervision_end_date_missing_include = ifelse(is.na(supervision_end_date)==TRUE,
                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date))),
         supervision_end_date_missing_include = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date_missing_include)),
         ### flag records with no joining violation information using violation_referral_number
         no_violation_records_joined = ifelse(is.na(violation_referral_number==TRUE),
                                       1,0),
         ### flag records with joining violation information using dates
         violation_records_are_joined = ifelse(violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include,
                                       1,0),
         ### create date field for technical violations only
         ### we'll use this when keeping the first technical violation per referral
         technical_violation_filed_date = ifelse(violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation",
                                                 violation_filed_date,
                                                 NA),
         technical_violation_filed_date = ymd(as_date(technical_violation_filed_date))) %>% 
        ### finally, create a flag for violation records that join 
        ### (i.e., youth has violation records), but
        ### do not have violations that fall within the given supervision period (for these records, we
        ### want to remove their violation data from the analytic file, 
        ### but ultimately keep all other data)
  mutate(has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag = ifelse(no_violation_records_joined==0 & (violation_date<supervision_begin_date | violation_date>supervision_end_date_missing_include),
                                                            1,0)) |> 
   ### recode all violation file values to NA if has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1
   ### this ensures that we do not accidentally use violation data for youth
   ### who only had violation that did not occur during the supervision periods in our sample (e.g., they had violations associated with supervision periods that occurred before the sample window)
  mutate(across(violation_referral_number:other_violation_count,
                ~ if_else(has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1,
                          NA, .))) %>%
  ### we only want to keep either (1) supervision records with no violations, (2) violation records that join (i.e., youth has violation records), but do not have violations that fall within the given supervision period, or (3) supervision records with violation records when those violations occurred during the period of supervision  
  filter(no_violation_records_joined==1 | has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1 | (violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include)) %>% 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id) %>% 
  ### now create these flags at the supervision episode level
  ### so that we can drop records from supervision episodes with joined violation records that fit criteria #2 above (e.g., youth has both historic and current violation records that joined. because we won't entirely drop the youth/supervision episode if we remove the historic records, we should drop the historic records and only keep violations which occurred during pertinent supervision episode)
  mutate(no_violation_records_joined_supervision_level = max(no_violation_records_joined),
         has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag_supervision_level = max(has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag),
         violation_records_are_joined_supervision_level = max(violation_records_are_joined)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  ### Question 1 from QA: 
  ### now create flag and filter on it -- based on above logic/rationale
  ### we want to drop joined records whose violation falls outside out of the given supervision episode (i.e., a violation that occurred before a supervision episode in our sample) if other violation data for that youth does fall within the supervision episode
  mutate(has_joined_violation_data_drop_record = ifelse(violation_records_are_joined_supervision_level==1 & has_violation_data_but_not_in_window_flag==1,
                                                        1,0)) |> 
  ### here, we are only keeping records where the flag we created based on these two variables is 0
  filter(has_joined_violation_data_drop_record==0) |> 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id) %>% 
  ### count of referrals linked to any violation (using no_violation_records_joined), technical violations, and new offense violations
  mutate(overall_violation_referral_count = n_distinct(violation_referral_number[no_violation_records_joined==0],
                                                         na.rm = TRUE),
         technical_violation_referral_count = n_distinct(violation_referral_number[no_violation_records_joined==0 & violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation"],
                                                         na.rm = TRUE),
         new_offense_violation_referral_count = n_distinct(violation_referral_number[no_violation_records_joined==0 & violation_severity_factor=="New Offense"],
                                                           na.rm = TRUE),
         min_technical_violation_date = min(technical_violation_filed_date,
                                            na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ### now de-dup by supervision record to get same row count as before join 
  ### first arrange by unique_supervision_id and violation date to keep first
  ### violation date
  arrange(unique_supervision_id,
          violation_filed_date) |> 
  distinct(unique_supervision_id,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  ### Question 2 from QA: look at supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall – how and where do I ensure that this is to first technical and not first overall violation?
  ### i need to create a flag indicating the order of violations and use a combination of this along with 
  ### violation severity == "Technical" to create `supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall`
  ### since we have de-duplicated by supervision episode -- keeping first violation
  ### if that first violation date is the same as the earliest technical violation date
  ### that we have recorded, the first violation is a technical violation
  ### we'll use this flag when creating `supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall` below
  mutate(first_violation_is_technical_violation = ifelse(violation_filed_date==min_technical_violation_date,
                                               1,0)) |> 
  ### now calculate time to first technical violation (with both vars)
  mutate(supervision_start_first_tech_violation_any = as.numeric(difftime(min_technical_violation_date,
                                                            supervision_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days")),
         supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall = as.numeric(difftime(violation_filed_date,
                                                            supervision_begin_date,
                                                                    units="days")),
         ### recode supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall as NA is first_violation_is_technical_violation != 1
         supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall = ifelse(first_violation_is_technical_violation==1,
                                                                       supervision_start_first_tech_violation_first_overall,NA)) |> 
  mutate(technical_violation_flag = ifelse(technical_violation_referral_count>0 & !is.na(overall_violation_referral_count)==TRUE,
                                           1,0),
         overall_violation_referral_flag = ifelse(overall_violation_referral_count>0 & !is.na(overall_violation_referral_count)==TRUE,
                                                  1,0))
```

```{.r .cell-code}
                supervision_level_phase_begin_date = phase_begin_date,

  ### create hierarchy of supervision levels
  ### when we measure changes/modifications to supervision levels,
  ### we are most interested in changes to more intensive levels of supervision

    mutate(supervision_level_phase_severity = 
           case_when(

  ### now arrange and group by youth to take the next supervision level, if present
  ### using dplyr::lead to take the next supervision_level_phase_severity value
  ### using https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/lead-lag.html
  ### this will allow us to calculate the number of instances where youth
```

```{.r .cell-code}
### Question 4 from QA: look into logic of modifications prior to first technical violation 
## I've double checked the logic and everything looks good:
## We first only keep violations + modification joins where either 
# (1) the violation occurs within the supervision episode (the modification file has episode start/end dates)
# or (2) there are no modifications to join to the violation data (our final analytic file here will have a 
# unit of analysis of first time technical violations)
## We then only keep modifications that occurred at least two days prior to the filed violation date
## We then only keep technical violations and modifications which represent an increase in intensiveness
## and finally use the `anti_join` function with the supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only dataframe
## to remove modifications that are actually linked to a new offense violation (and we don't want to accidentally
## count as a sanction unrelated to any violation)

### next join violations_clean_de_dup and supervision_level_clean_to_join_modifications_violations
### to create main analytic file for this question of modifications prior to technical violation
### we will eventually 
modification_prior_to_technical_violation_count <- 
  left_join(violations_clean_de_dup,
            supervision_level_clean_to_join_modifications_violations,
            by = c("unique_id")) %>% ### this is a many to many join so there are now lots of records (all violations joining to all supervisions/supervision extensions/supervision levels)
  ### now we need to filter on date -- only keeping violation records where the violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date
  ### first create fake end date for records where the end date is blank; since this indicates that supervision was ongoing at time of data pull, we still want to include violations that occurred so changing NA to '2030-01-01' in new variable for the following filter
  mutate(supervision_end_date_missing_include = ifelse(is.na(supervision_end_date)==TRUE,
                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date))),
         violation_date = ymd(as_date(violation_date)),
         ### create var with day subtracted for modification date logic (as extra buffer)
         ### business rule: modification phase date must be less than violation date -1 day
         violation_date_plus_one_day = violation_date - lubridate::days(1),
         violation_date_missing_include = ifelse(is.na(violation_date)==TRUE,
                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(violation_date))),
         supervision_end_date_missing_include = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date_missing_include)),
         ### flag records with no joining modification information using supervision_level_phase_begin_date
         no_modification_records_joined = ifelse(is.na(supervision_level_phase_begin_date==TRUE),
                                       1,0)) %>% 
  ### for this analysis, our denominator will be violations (e.g., % of violations with modifications prior to first, etc.)
  ### so we only want to keep either (1) violation records with no modifications or (2) supervision records with violation records when those violations occurred during the period of supervision  
  ### we only want records that fit our criteria of:
  ### violations occurring during the supervision episode
  ### so we are dropping violations here that occurred outside sample window for supervision episodes (FY 2018 through FY 2023)
  filter(no_modification_records_joined==1 | (violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include)) %>% 
  ### only technical violations (given that we're exploring the % of violations
  ### with modifications prior to first)
  ### and only modifications which mark an increase in intensiveness
  filter(violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation",
          supervision_level_is_increase_flag==1) %>% 
  ### for this analysis, keep first violation per supervision episode (b/c we're
  ### only interested in the % of first technical violation where a modification
  ### occurred prior)
  ### de-dup, keeping first record to preserve violation and linked modifications for supervision period
  ### also keep earliest supervision_level_phase_begin_date that joined
  arrange(unique_supervision_id,
          violation_date,
          supervision_level_phase_begin_date) %>%
  distinct(unique_supervision_id,
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  ### and modifications occurring before the violation
  ### and only modifications that were increases in intensiveness
  ### when we de-dup, we will keep first violation per supervision episode
  filter(no_modification_records_joined==1 | (supervision_level_phase_begin_date<violation_date_plus_one_day)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(unique_id,
                violation_referral_number,
                referral_number,
                unique_supervision_id,
                violation,
                violation_date,
                violation_date_plus_one_day,
                supervision_begin_date,
                supervision_end_date,
                supervision_end_date_missing_include,
                supervision_level_phase,
                supervision_level_phase_begin_date,
                supervision_level_phase_end_date,
                supervision_level_is_increase_flag) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(unique_modification_id = paste0(unique_supervision_id,
                                         supervision_level_phase_begin_date,
                                         supervision_level_phase_end_date)) |> 
  ### anti-join modification_prior_to_technical_violation_count and supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only 
  ### keeping only modification records which appear in modification_prior_to_technical_violation_count BUT not in supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only
  ### this removes modification records linked to new offenses from our file
  ### which we don't want (given that we're exploring modifications used as sanctions
  ### but not linked to formal violations)
  anti_join(supervision_modification_new_offense_violations_only,
            by = "unique_modification_id") |> 
  group_by(unique_supervision_id,
          violation_date) %>%
  ### at this point, we only have records that fit our criteria of 
  ### technical violations occurring during the supervision episode
  ### modifications occurring before the violation
  ### and only modifications that were increases in intensiveness
  ### when we de-dup, we will keep first violation per supervision episode
  ### now count modifications per violations
  mutate(modification_increase_prior_to_technical_count = n_distinct(unique_id,
                                                  unique_supervision_id,
                                                  supervision_level_phase,
                                                  supervision_level_phase_begin_date)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
 
  dplyr::select(unique_supervision_id,
                modification_increase_prior_to_technical_count)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
### this demo only file still has some duplicates (~500 youth have multiple records)
### for youth with multiple referrals
### we cannot simply de-dup because some variables, like age and risk/needs scores,
### are likely to change between records and we ultimately want to join the most pertinent/
### proximate record

### left join of violations_clean_de_dup file and df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file_demo_only file 
### because the referral number in the violations file refers to the new referral
### while the referral number in the overall analytic file refers to the original 
### referral, we can only join on youth ID
### and then use dates to link one demo record to each violation record
df_violations_clean_demo <- 
  left_join(violations_clean_de_dup,
            df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file_demo_only,
            by = "unique_id") |> 
  ### this is a many to many join so there are now lots of records (all violations joining to all demo records)
  ### first create fake end date for records where the end date is blank; since this indicates that supervision was ongoing at time of data pull, we still want to include violations that occurred so changing NA to '2030-01-01' in new variable for the following filter
  mutate(supervision_end_date_missing_include = ifelse(is.na(supervision_end_date)==TRUE,
                                       ymd(as_date("2030-01-01")),
                                       ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date))),
         supervision_end_date_missing_include = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date_missing_include)),
         supervision_begin_date = ymd(as_date(supervision_begin_date)),
         violation_date = ymd(as_date(violation_date))) %>% 
  ### now we need to filter on date -- only keeping demo records where the violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date
  ### we are also only keeping violations that occurred during sample window for supervision episodes (FY 2018 through FY 2023)
  filter(violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date_missing_include) |> 
  ### double check that we joined demo data to all violation records
  ### no records dropped so we did
  filter(!is.na(race_clean)) |> 
  ### now de-dup by violation to double check record count
  distinct(unique_violation_referral_id,
           .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
### BUSINESS RULE: Join extension and violations file on extension begin date and violation disposition date where dates are -1 day or +3 days within each other) (time from violation_disposition_date to supervision_extension_begin_date)

### left join of supervision_extension_for_join_to_violations_clean file and df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file_demo_only file 
supervision_extension_demo_violations_analysis_clean <- 
  left_join(supervision_extension_for_join_to_violations_clean,
            df_violations_clean_demo,
            by = c("unique_id")) |> 
  ### filter on technical violations only
  filter(violation_severity_factor=="Technical Violation") |> 
   ### clean dates and create years for potential grouping in future trend analysis
  mutate(supervision_extension_begin_date = ymd(as_date(supervision_extension_begin_date)),
         violation_disposition_date = ymd(as_date(violation_disposition_date)),
         time_from_violation_dispo_to_extension_days = as.numeric(difftime(supervision_extension_begin_date,
                                                            violation_disposition_date,
                                                                    units="days"))) |> 
  ### we are only keeping joins where the time from violation_disposition_date to supervision_extension_begin_date
  filter(time_from_violation_dispo_to_extension_days>-1,
         time_from_violation_dispo_to_extension_days<=3) |> 
  ### double check that we joined demo data to all violation records
  ### we did
  filter(!is.na(race_clean)) |> 
  ### now de-dup by extension to double check record count
  mutate(unique_supervision_extension = paste0(unique_supervision_id,
                                               supervision_extension_begin_date)) |> 
  ### for the remaining duplicates, arrange by extension record
  ### keeping demo data associated with original entry (earliest supervision_begin_date)
  arrange(unique_supervision_extension,
          supervision_begin_date) |> 
  distinct(unique_supervision_extension,
           .keep_all = TRUE) ### our final file size is now smaller b/c we have (in theory) dropped all agreed order supervision extensions (and are only left with extensions resulting from technical or new offense violations) (1528/1814 = 84%)
```
